evaluated.name: IntangibleWeightedAccrualOverhang
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(xrd, sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The total-accrual anomaly is strongest where earnings are hardest to verify; R&D-intensive firms have opaque revenue recognition and long payoff horizons, so a given dollar of accrual-based (non-cash) earnings is more likely to reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: The accrual wedge (ib minus oancf) is signed and standardized, then amplified by the firm's rank in R&D intensity, so the signal is large-positive only for intangible-intensive firms whose earnings are accrual-driven. Pure R&D intensity alone carries no directional bet here because the RANK term only scales the accrual channel, forcing a genuine interaction rather than a single-theme effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcquiredIntangibleAccrualInflation
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(intan, at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: When a firm expands its capitalized intangible base (acquisitions, capitalized development, purchase-price allocation), the acquired operations arrive with receivables and inventory that are recognized before cash conversion is verified; working-capital accruals booked during intangible expansion are therefore far more likely to reverse than the same accruals at a stable-intangible firm.
evaluated.reasoning: The accrual leg is kept in its standard asset-scaled form (no deflator surgery, so no small-denominator instability), and the intangible theme enters as a bounded 0-1 conditioning weight on the change in intangible share, which is the purchase-accounting channel rather than the R&D-expense channel used in the accepted signal. The signal is near zero for firms with flat intangible intensity regardless of their accruals, so the bet is explicitly on accruals generated inside intangible expansion rather than on the Sloan effect itself.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashQualityWeightedRnDGrowth
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(GROWTH(RATIO(xrd, at), 1), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: An increase in R&D intensity is informative about future productivity only when reported earnings are cash-backed; when the same firm is simultaneously accruing income it cannot collect, the R&D increase is far more likely to be an accounting or window-dressing artifact than a credible commitment of resources.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the additive SUMRANK with a genuine conditional structure: the signed, standardized R&D-intensity change is the bet, and the accrual rank is a bounded 0-1 gate that shrinks the bet toward zero for accrual-heavy firms. The claimed interaction is now literally what the algebra does — high R&D growth pays only with clean accruals, and R&D contraction is treated as informative only for firms whose earnings are cash-verified.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualBetGatedByRnDIntensity
evaluated.expression: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(xrd, at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(xrd, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual mispricing requires information opacity; among R&D-intensive firms investors cannot separate expensed intangible investment from discretionary accrual choices, so the accrual-return relation should be strong there and essentially absent among tangible, easily audited firms.
evaluated.reasoning: The min-of-ranks construction makes the accrual spread mechanically widen with R&D intensity: for a top-R&D firm the expression reduces to a full clean-minus-dirty accrual bet, while for a near-zero-R&D firm the two MIN terms cancel and the signal collapses to zero. This removes the 1/R&D domination of the flagged ratio version — R&D never appears in a denominator and low-R&D firms are placed in the neutral middle rather than the long tail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualUptrendAgainstRnDDowntrend
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5), 1)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(xrd, sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms harvesting accounting earnings from a shrinking innovation base are the clearest case of accrual-driven rather than productive earnings: a multi-year rise in the accrual share of income combined with a multi-year decline in R&D intensity signals substitution of accounting income for real intangible investment, and both components reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: The near-constant TS_COUNT leg is dropped entirely, so nothing collapses to plain R&D intensity; instead both themes enter as five-year directional states, with the signed accrual trend as the bet and the R&D-intensity downtrend rank as the conditioning weight. Firms whose intangible commitment is rising receive near-zero weight even with rising accruals, which is the divergence concept the earlier version only claimed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SlowAmortizationIntangibleOverhang
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(intan, at)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The non-cash charge dp is the accrual through which capitalized intangibles are expensed; an intangible-heavy balance sheet carried with unusually light depreciation and amortization means the intangible stock is being written off too slowly, inflating current earnings and storing up impairment risk.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the deflator-swap logic and the ceq denominator entirely — no small or negative scaler appears, since both legs are scaled by total assets and one leg is a bounded rank. The economic content is a true cross-theme conjunction: low amortization intensity is only diagnostic when there is a large capitalized intangible stock to amortize, so tangible firms with low dp/at receive near-zero signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossMarginGatedAccrualOverhang
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross margin is a full-sample proxy for knowledge/brand capital that is expensed rather than capitalized: high-margin firms earn rents from intangibles that never appear on the balance sheet, and their earnings are correspondingly harder to audit, so accrual-driven income reverses more strongly there than at low-margin, tangible processing firms.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the xrd gate (coverage 0.047) with an intangible-rent proxy available for essentially every firm, so the same conditional mechanism as the accepted gen-0 winner can be tested with roughly ten times the observations. The accrual leg is industry-z-scored so the long-short spread is not simply a bet on high-margin industries, which is the composition problem that killed the SlowAmortization alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ReceivableBuildupInIntangibleFirms
evaluated.expression: MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(recch, at), 1))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(intan, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: For intangible-intensive firms, revenue recognition is the softest accounting margin: licensing, milestone, and multi-element software or pharma contracts let a firm book sales into receivables long before cash arrives, so receivable build-up specifically (not the whole accrual aggregate) marks accounting-driven rather than productive earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the accrual channel from the aggregate ib-minus-oancf wedge to a single cash-flow-statement component whose economic story is tied directly to intangible business models, so it teaches something the aggregate-accrual family cannot. The intangible gate combines capitalized intangibles with expensed R&D so both the acquisition and the research routes to intangible intensity count.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IntangibleCapitalGatedByCashEarnings
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The undervaluation of expensed intangible capital should be concentrated in firms whose reported earnings are cash-backed; when a research-intensive firm is simultaneously accruing uncollected income, the market's discount is justified rather than a mispricing, so the intangible-capital premium is earned only in the accrual-clean subset.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-0 showed the intangible leg fails as a growth bet (CashQualityWeightedRnDGrowth, wrong-signed alpha), so here the bet is the five-year R&D capital stock — a slow-moving state variable with a documented value channel — gated by a bounded earnings-quality rank. The zero convention for non-reporters keeps the low-intangible control group in the sample and lifts coverage well above the 0.037 of the failed growth version.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DeferredGoodwillImpairmentAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(MUL(RATIO(gdwl, at), NEG(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Goodwill impairment is the most discretionary write-down in accounting; when a goodwill-heavy firm's revenue is shrinking, economic impairment has occurred, and management can postpone recognizing it while simultaneously supporting reported income with positive accruals — earnings that must reverse through both accrual reversal and an eventual write-off.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons dp, which the critic correctly notes is dominated by PP&E depreciation and therefore proxies capital intensity rather than intangible write-off policy, and replaces it with the specific intangible account whose non-recognition is discretionary (gdwl) conditioned on the state that makes impairment due (falling sales). The bet remains the signed, industry-neutral accrual wedge, so the portfolio is not a static goodwill or capital-intensity tilt but a bet on firms deferring bad news on two accounting margins at once.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualBoostWithIntangibleExpenseCut
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, xad), sale), 1), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms manage earnings on two margins simultaneously: accrual manipulation and real cuts to discretionary intangible-building expense (R&D or advertising). A firm that raises accrual-based income in the same year it cuts intangible expense intensity is buying reported earnings twice over, sacrificing future intangible capital, so its earnings are least persistent.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than using intangible intensity as a static opacity gate — which at full coverage degenerates into plain Sloan, as the critic notes — the intangible leg here is a *change* in discretionary intangible spending, a real-earnings-management action that only interacts with accruals when both move to inflate income. COALESCE(xrd, xad) uses whichever discretionary intangible expense the firm actually reports as its primary brand/knowledge investment, giving materially wider coverage than xrd alone without turning the gate into a constant.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: StableAccrualIntangibleIntensity
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(intan, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible intensity per se is not informative — what matters is whether the intangible program is accompanied by quiet or noisy accounting. Intangible-intensive firms whose accrual wedge is stable over five years are running genuine investment programs whose expensing depresses reported earnings mechanically, while equally intangible-intensive firms with volatile accruals are producing accounting-driven earnings the market cannot decode.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a second-moment interaction, not another level bet or subsample filter: the intangible rank supplies the population where accounting noise matters and the signed accrual-volatility z-score supplies the quality discrimination within it, so neither leg alone spans the signal. It directly implements the task's "separate productive intangible investment from accounting-driven earnings" framing and is the only proposal in the archive whose accrual channel is a dispersion rather than a level.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BroadIntangibleCapitalCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Total intangible capital is the sum of the internally generated stock (five years of expensed R&D) and the purchased stock on the balance sheet; the market underprices this combined capital only when reported earnings are cash-backed, because accrual-supported earnings make the intangible story indistinguishable from accounting inflation.
evaluated.reasoning: This extends the archive's best signal (alpha +5.2%, t = 3.0) by measuring intangible capital through both the expensing and the capitalization route, so firms that build intangibles by acquisition are no longer scored as zero-intangible controls. The bet leg is industry-demeaned so the long portfolio is not simply a pharma/software basket, which should convert some of the raw spread into FF5 alpha and lift the currently weak FMB slope.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ChronicCleanAccrualIntangibleCapital
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year of low accruals can be noise or a timing artifact; what certifies an intangible investment program is a multi-year record of converting reported income into cash, so the intangible-capital premium should be earned by firms with persistently, not momentarily, clean accruals.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates exactly one design choice relative to IntangibleCapitalGatedByCashEarnings — the accrual gate's measurement window (1 year versus a 3-year average) — holding the bet leg, scaling, and coverage convention fixed. If the alpha rises, the mechanism is earnings-quality persistence; if it falls, the gate is capturing a transient accrual-reversal effect, and either outcome directs later consolidation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WithinIndustryIntangibleGatedAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes accruals hard to interpret is a firm being intangible-intensive *relative to its industry peers*, not relative to the whole market: an average software firm is transparent to a software analyst, whereas an unusually intangible-heavy industrial firm has genuinely unfamiliar accounting.
evaluated.reasoning: The market-wide gross-margin gate diluted the effect (t = -1.1) because it re-sorted the entire market into industries rather than discriminating within them; an industry-relative intangible gate keeps the gate informative while preserving near-full coverage through the zero conventions. This repairs the coverage weakness of the 0.047-coverage gen-0 winner without collapsing into plain Sloan, since the weight still varies sharply within every industry.

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryAccrualSpikeIntangibleFirms
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cross-sectional accrual levels confound business model with manipulation — some firms are structurally accrual-heavy. An accrual reading that is extreme relative to the firm's own five-year history is the manipulation signal, and it is least detectable, hence most mispriced, at intangible-intensive firms whose fundamentals are hard to benchmark.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg in the archive has been a cross-sectional level or trend; this substitutes a firm-relative position measure, which removes the permanent business-model component and isolates the transitory accounting decision. Because the mechanism differs from prior tests only in the accrual leg's frame of reference, a strong result would tell us the mispricing is about abnormal accounting behaviour rather than accrual level, a lesson no existing archive entry can deliver.

evaluated.name: BrandCapitalCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 5), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Advertising builds brand capital that is fully expensed exactly like R&D, so if the intangible-capital premium is really about expensed investment being missing from book value, it should appear in accumulated advertising too — and again only where earnings are cash-backed rather than accrual-supported.
evaluated.reasoning: This is an out-of-channel replication of the archive's best mechanism using a different expensed intangible, which is the sharpest available test of whether that alpha reflects expensing-driven mispricing or something specific to R&D-intensive tech and pharma. A positive result would justify combining both stocks in later generations; a null would tell us the effect is innovation-specific and should be refined on the R&D side only.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorkingCapitalBloatAtIntangibleFirms
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 3), 1)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A multi-year rise in working capital per dollar of revenue means the firm's growth is being carried by uncollected receivables and unsold inventory rather than by cash conversion; at intangible-intensive firms this chronic bloat is the clearest evidence that the intangible program is producing accounting revenue rather than productive output, and it precedes both accrual reversals and write-offs.
evaluated.reasoning: The abandoned big-bath construction was algebraically a mix of an archived signal and vanilla Sloan, so this replaces the accrual leg entirely with a variable and a normalization the archive has never used — the wcap level scaled by sales, measured as a three-year trend rather than a one-year change — which is a chronic operating-asset-bloat concept, not a one-period accrual. The intangible leg stays the stock measure that has actually worked in evaluation (capitalized intangibles plus five-year R&D capital), so the interaction asks a new question: does cash-conversion deterioration matter more where the asset base is intangible and unverifiable?
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RankedChronicAccrualIntangibleGate
evaluated.expression: RANK(MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Chronic accrual-supported earnings, not a single year's accrual, is what intangible-intensive firms use to substitute accounting income for verifiable output; the mispricing should therefore be measured on a smoothed accrual state, and the resulting portfolio bet should be read from the firm's rank rather than from a fat-tailed product.
evaluated.reasoning: This carries the one lever that demonstrably improved the positive side (3-year accrual averaging) over to the best negative-side signal, and wraps the composite in a monotone RANK so the Fama-MacBeth slope is not attenuated by extreme product values — the decile portfolios and hence the alpha are unaffected by the rank transform, so this specifically targets the archive's persistent fmb/alpha divergence.

evaluated.name: IntangibleAdjustedGrossProfitCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment shows up as gross profit generated per dollar of intangible-augmented capital; the market rewards this only when the profit is cash-backed, because gross profitability at chronically accrual-heavy firms is itself an artifact of revenue recognition rather than of output.
evaluated.reasoning: Every prior bet leg has been an input measure (how much intangible capital the firm holds); this is the first output measure — the return on that capital — which directly implements the task's mandate to separate productive intangible investment from accounting-driven earnings. Capitalizing R&D into the denominator makes the profitability metric comparable across expensing regimes, so the interaction is intrinsic rather than a bolted-on gate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InternalMinusAcquiredIntangibleCapital
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: How a firm builds intangible capital matters more than how much it holds: internally generated R&D capital is expensed and therefore invisible in book value, whereas acquired goodwill is capitalized at a negotiated price that already embeds a control premium and is systematically over-stated. Firms that are deep in the invisible kind and light in the purchased kind, and whose earnings are chronically cash-backed, are the ones the market misvalues.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not the additive ablation the critic rejected — the two intangible stocks enter with opposite signs, making the bet a contrast between modes of intangible creation rather than a broader measure of the same thing. It also gives the short leg a coherent identity for the first time in this family (goodwill-heavy, R&D-light, accrual-supported roll-ups), which the pure R&D-stock winner never had.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PreRnDEconomicEarningsCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Reported income understates the economic profitability of research-intensive firms because R&D is a discretionary investment charged against current earnings; profitability measured before the intangible investment charge is the true productive-capacity measure, and it is credible only where the accrual record shows the income converts to cash.
evaluated.reasoning: The bet leg changes from an intangible *stock* to an expensing-corrected *earnings* concept, so this asks a different economic question than the archived winner — whether mispricing comes from unbooked capital or from understated current profitability — and the two can be told apart by their alphas. Smoothing profitability over three years matches the gate's horizon and avoids one-year expense timing artifacts.

evaluated.name: DiscretionaryAccrualGatedRnDCapital
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Depreciation and amortization are non-discretionary accruals that make ib − oancf mechanically negative for capital-intensive firms, so the standard wedge grades firms by capital intensity as much as by earnings quality; adding dp back isolates the working-capital accruals management actually chooses, which is the component that reverses.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs a measurement flaw the critic identified in the gate itself rather than swapping a scaler on the bet leg: with D&A stripped out, the gate ranks firms by discretionary accounting behaviour instead of by asset composition, which should sharpen the contrast between productive intangible investors and accrual-driven earnings. It also removes the mechanical negative correlation between the gate and any capital-intensity content in the R&D-capital bet leg.

evaluated.name: ConjunctiveIntangibleEarningsQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The premium requires both conditions simultaneously — deep expensed intangible capital and chronically cash-backed earnings — so a firm should be scored by its weaker dimension; a research-heavy firm with soft earnings and a cash-clean firm with no intangible capital are both uninteresting, and neither deserves a large positive score.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the miscalibrated hard sign gate with a conjunction that has no threshold, no zero mass, and no tie clusters, so decile portfolios stay well populated while the long leg is forced to satisfy both criteria jointly. Comparing it against the multiplicative form on identical inputs answers a structural question the archive has not settled — whether the interaction is graded and multiplicative or limited by the weaker channel.

evaluated.name: TripleGateIntangibleQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Separating productive intangible investment from accounting-driven earnings requires three simultaneous conditions: the firm must actually hold deep expensed intangible capital, that capital must generate economic (pre-R&D) profits, and those profits must convert to cash. Failing any one condition disqualifies the firm.
evaluated.reasoning: The two-way conjunction already improved on the multiplicative form, so the open question is whether adding the pre-R&D economic-earnings channel — which carried the archive's best FMB slope of 4.05 — sharpens the long leg further or merely thins it. Nested MINs keep every input on a common bounded scale, and the outcome tells us whether the mechanism is about capital, about returns on that capital, or about both.

evaluated.name: PureAccrualInteractionWithinIntangibleFirms
evaluated.expression: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the effect is a true interaction, the accrual spread should widen monotonically with intangible-capital depth and vanish among firms with no expensed intangible capital, so a signal that mechanically nets out the intangible main effect should still carry alpha.

evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The short side of the mechanism is firms that are simultaneously intangible-heavy and chronically accrual-supported: their asset base cannot be verified and their earnings do not convert to cash, so both the reported profits and the intangible story unwind.

evaluated.hypothesis: Both intangible depth and earnings quality are only interpretable against industry norms — a 3%-of-assets R&D stock is deep for a manufacturer and trivial for a biotech, and accrual conventions differ by business model — so the mispriced firms are those that are unusual on both dimensions relative to their peers.

evaluated.name: TaxConfirmedEarningsAtIntangibleFirms
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), at), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Income the firm is willing to pay tax on is income it cannot easily fabricate: a rise in taxes payable is an externally disciplined confirmation that reported profits are real. It keeps the bounded conjunctive structure that produced the archive's best portfolio evidence while asking a genuinely different question: is the earnings-quality gate about cash conversion specifically, or about any externally verified confirmation of income?

considered.hypothesis: Some business models are permanently accrual-intensive, which is information about industry structure rather than about accounting behaviour; what signals manipulation is an accrual reading that is high relative to the firm's own five-year record, and that escalation is least detectable — hence most mispriced — at firms whose asset base is dominated by capitalized intangibles carried at management's estimates.
considered.reasoning: The sign conflict in the acquisitive-story signal is better explained by the revenue-decline leg acting as a value/distress proxy, which carries a positive cross-sectional return relation and fights the intended sign, than by any tie structure; I therefore remove that leg entirely rather than change the operator. Framing the accrual leg in firm-relative terms strips out the permanent business-model component that the cross-sectional level confounds with industry and value exposure, so the remaining variation is the transitory accounting decision the hypothesis is actually about.

considered.name: DoubleGatedVersusCashBurningIntangibleSpread
considered.expression: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))))))
considered.hypothesis: The two populations that should diverge are research-intensive firms whose cash generation and conservative reporting both certify the invisible capital, and acquisition-built intangible firms that consume cash even before research while booking income they do not collect; the second group's assets are management estimates supported by accruals rather than by operations.
considered.reasoning: The short corner here is new — it screens on *purchased* intangibles and pre-research cash burn rather than the archived pre-R&D-ROA screen — so the spread is not a recombination of two evaluated signals, and its intangible leg differs from the long corner's, which prevents the spread from collapsing into an accrual bet within one population. The deliberate appearance of cash flow with opposite orientation on the two sides is the economic content, not an artifact: the long corner requires cash generation, the short corner requires cash consumption, and these identify disjoint firms.

considered.name: CashBurningAcquiredIntangibleAccruals
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: The clearest overvalued profile is a balance sheet dominated by purchased intangibles at a firm that consumes cash in operations and reports earnings well above its cash flow: the assets rest on estimates, the income rests on accruals, and operations fund neither.
considered.reasoning: This is the short corner of Signal 2 evaluated standalone, which is necessary to attribute any spread improvement to the corner rather than to the long side, and it is a materially different short screen from the archived one because it substitutes cash burn for accounting unprofitability and purchased intangibles for the combined stock. The archived short corner reached fmb -2.52 and alpha -6.0%; if this exceeds that, the final specification should adopt it, and if not, the spread should keep the profitability-based screen.

considered.name: HiddenCapitalShareCashGated
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ABS(ceq), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: What the market must fail to capitalize is intangible capital relative to the equity investors actually observe, not relative to total assets; the share of a firm's true equity base that is invisible — accumulated research divided by visible plus invisible equity — is the direct measure of that gap, and it is only informative where operations generate cash before research.
considered.reasoning: The equity-scaled version of the bet leg was blocked earlier because negative or near-zero book equity inverts the ratio's sign; taking the absolute value of equity in the denominator and forming a bounded share in [0,1] removes that hazard entirely while preserving the value-relevant interpretation. This tests whether the premium is about capital hidden from the equity base — the mechanism the literature attributes it to — rather than about asset-light business models, which is the last unresolved economic question about the bet leg.

considered.name: WorkingCapitalAccrualCoverageExtendedGate
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, SUB(ADD(ib, dp), SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))))), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, COALESCE(oancf, SUB(ADD(ib, dp), SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)))))), dp), at), 1), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: The discretionary part of the earnings-minus-cash wedge is the working-capital accrual, not depreciation, which is a mechanical function of past capital spending; defining the earnings-quality gate as the wedge with depreciation added back gives a measure with the same economic meaning — accruals management chooses — whether the firm's cash flow is observed or reconstructed from the balance sheet.
considered.reasoning: The critic is right that under reconstruction the raw wedge degenerates into a depreciation-intensity screen; adding dp back makes the gate identically the working-capital accrual on the reconstructed branch and the depreciation-adjusted wedge on the observed branch, so the construct is internally consistent across the whole sample. This is not a mechanical merge but a corrected definition — the dp-adjusted accrual was itself evaluated and worked (alpha 4.9%, t = 3.15) — and it is the only route to carrying the leading triple-gate specification to the 0.13 coverage the reconstruction unlocked.

considered.name: GeometricConjunctionIntangibleCashQuality
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Intangible depth and pre-research cash generation reinforce each other multiplicatively: each additional unit of invisible capital is worth more at a firm that demonstrably converts operations into cash, and cash generation is worth more where there is unbooked capital for the market to overlook.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the additive composite the critic rejected with a genuine interaction that is nonetheless bounded — the product of two rank variables — a form the archive has never tested, since every earlier multiplicative signal multiplied a fat-tailed signed z-score by a rank and was dominated by tail outliers. It sits strictly between the binding-constraint MIN and the substitutable additive form: it requires both conditions like MIN, but unlike MIN it does not discard information above the weaker rank, which should populate the long tail more finely and could lift both the FMB slope and the spread.

considered.name: ErodingRentsWithAccrualSupportAtIntangibleFirms
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 1))), RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Capitalized intangibles are only worth their carrying value while they generate pricing power; a firm whose gross margin is eroding has lost the rents that justified the intangible asset, and if it simultaneously supports reported income with accruals it is deferring both the impairment and the accrual reversal.
considered.reasoning: This is not the gen-0 acquisition-accrual mechanism recast — no intangible growth term appears — but a rent-erosion mechanism, using the change in gross margin, which was validated as an intangible-rent proxy on the long side (fmb 3.75) and has never been used in a short construct. It also avoids the flaw that produced the wrong-signed FMB slope in the fading-revenue screen, because margin compression is a measure of competitive position rather than a value/distress proxy the way negative sales growth is.

considered.name: BalanceSheetAccrualCashBurnIntangibleShort
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: An acquisition-built intangible balance sheet, an expanding stock of uncollected working-capital claims, and operations that consume cash before research spending are three separately verifiable symptoms of value that exists only on paper.
considered.reasoning: The current best short leg conditions on ib − oancf and on oancf + xrd, which are largely the same low-cash-flow condition, so its apparent three-way screen is partly a double count; replacing the wedge with the noncash, debt-excluded balance-sheet accrual makes the accrual condition independent of the cash condition. If the alpha survives at similar magnitude, the short-side mechanism is genuinely multidimensional and the spread built on it is not merely a cash-flow bet — the specific objection raised against the leading spread.

considered.name: DepreciationAdjustedDoubleGateStandardSample
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), 1), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Only the working-capital portion of the earnings-minus-cash wedge reflects accounting discretion; depreciation is a mechanical consequence of past capital expenditure, so removing it should sharpen the earnings-quality gate for intangible-intensive firms whose asset composition differs systematically from the market.
considered.reasoning: The coverage-extended signal changed two things at once — the sample and the depreciation adjustment — and delivered the best ls_talpha in the archive, so this runs the depreciation adjustment alone on the standard sample to attribute the gain. The answer determines the final recommended specification: if this matches or beats the unadjusted double gate at 0.091 coverage, the dp adjustment is a genuine improvement rather than an artifact of the extended sample.

considered.name: DiscretionaryAccrualTwoCornerIntangibleSpread
considered.expression: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), 1), 3))))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))))))
considered.hypothesis: Depreciation is not an accounting choice, so the discretionary accrual is the wedge with D&A added back; a research-deep firm that generates cash and keeps discretionary accruals conservative is the productive pole, while an acquisition-built intangible balance sheet expanding its working-capital claims while burning cash is the accounting-driven pole.
considered.reasoning: I drop the balance-sheet reconstruction, which the critic correctly showed makes the long corner's two gates algebraic rearrangements of one another for the reconstructed third of the sample, and instead sharpen the long corner by replacing the raw wedge with the D&A-adjusted discretionary accrual — a different quantity from the level of pre-research cash flow rather than its mirror image. The short corner is deliberately measured on the balance sheet, so the spread contrasts two populations diagnosed from different accounting surfaces, which is what the previous version claimed but did not deliver.

considered.name: ImprovingCashConversionOfResearchCapital
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 5), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accumulated research is worth most when its payoff phase has begun: a firm whose pre-research cash generation is not only high but rising over five years is converting past intangible investment into operating cash, whereas a high but flattening level may reflect a mature franchise the market has already capitalized.
considered.reasoning: Every gate tested so far is a level or a smoothed level; the direction of change in cash conversion is an economically distinct state — the transition from investment to harvest — and it is the natural dynamic complement to a stock-based intangible bet, which is why it is worth the final slot rather than another rescaling. It also addresses the one weakness of the leading long corner, which cannot distinguish a franchise whose research is currently paying off from one whose cash generation is decaying.

considered.name: PeerRelativeCashGenerationIntangibleQuality
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Cash-generation norms are set by industry technology and contracting — biotech, enterprise software and specialty pharma have structurally different pre-research cash margins — so what certifies an intangible program is generating more cash than its own peers, whereas the intangible stock itself is mispriced relative to the whole market because investors under-capitalize expensed investment everywhere.
considered.reasoning: The industry question was previously tested only by demeaning every leg at once, which conflated the bet and the gate; here the bet leg stays market-wide, where the expensing mispricing lives, while only the certification gate becomes peer-relative, which is where industry technology genuinely determines the benchmark. This is a substantive economic distinction between where industry structure matters and where it does not, and it can raise both the slope and the alpha by removing sector composition from the gate without discarding the cross-industry intangible tilt that drives the premium.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PricingPowerAndCashBackedIntangibleCapital
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Productive intangible investment must show up as pricing power in the product market and as cash in the operating accounts; a deep research stock that produces neither is a cost centre, and gross margin measures the rent the intangible asset earns while pre-research cash flow measures whether that rent is collected.
considered.reasoning: Gross margin is a revenue-side measure of intangible rents that is not collinear with either the research stock or cash generation — unlike the two scalings of the same numerator the critic rejected — and it delivered fmb 3.75 when paired with the accrual gate but has never been combined with the stronger cash gate. This asks the final open economic question of the search: whether the premium requires evidence of rents in the product market on top of evidence of cash in the accounts.

critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent (signed z-scored accruals scaled by a non-negative R&D rank preserves the negative expected sign) and it implements a genuine conditional bet rather than an additive blend, though the "accrual anomaly is stronger under high information uncertainty/intangible intensity" conditioning is close to published territory and the multiplicative rank weight compresses low-R&D firms toward zero, so coverage and long-leg stability should be checked.

This is the standard Sloan working-capital accrual anomaly with a denominator swap (at minus intan), a cosmetic rescaling that adds no cross-theme mechanism and risks instability for goodwill-heavy firms where the tangible base is small.

SUMRANK is an additive rank average, so the stated "firms high on only one leg are pushed to the middle" interaction logic is wrong — it is a linear composite of two separately published anomalies (R&D increases and accruals) with no conditional structure.

Dividing a signed accrual ratio by a small positive R&D intensity makes the signal dominated by 1/R&D rather than by accruals — low-R&D firms with mildly negative accruals land in the extreme long tail, contradicting the stated hypothesis, and 1% winsorization will not fix the non-monotonicity.

TS_COUNT is near-constant (≈5) for continuous R&D reporters so the first leg collapses to plain R&D/assets, making this an additive combination of the known R&D-intensity and earnings-stability effects rather than the "state-quality" interaction claimed.

Another accrual deflator swap that duplicates the logic of TangibleBaseAccrualIntensity, and because ceq can be small or negative the ratio flips sign for exactly the distressed/intangible-heavy firms the hypothesis targets, breaking the monotonic mapping to the expected negative slope.

Internally consistent (non-negative rank weight preserves the accrual sign, so negative expected sign is right) and the gross-margin-as-unbooked-intangible-rents gate is a defensible, high-coverage substitute for the sparse R&D gate rather than a cosmetic re-run, though one should verify the result is not just the plain Sloan accrual effect surviving a near-uniform weight.

This is a near-mechanical industry-demeaned re-run of the archived SlowAmortizationIntangibleOverhang, and the underlying mechanism is weak because dp is dominated by PP&E depreciation rather than intangible amortization, so the "under-amortization" story is largely a capital-intensity tilt that industry-neutralizing may simply neutralize away rather than convert into alpha.

With COALESCE(xrd,0) the gate becomes nearly uniform across the (majority) non-reporting firms and the signal collapses toward the plain accrual anomaly at full coverage — a direct rediscovery of Sloan (1996) — and it changes two things at once (missing-data convention *and* ZSCORE→IND_ZSCORE) so it does not cleanly isolate the design choice it claims to test.

Decomposing the accrual wedge into the receivable channel and tying it to a revenue-recognition story specific to intangible-intensive business models is a genuinely different and testable mechanism, with the caveat that the whole sign hinges on recch following the Compustat "decrease(increase)" convention (negative when receivables build), which must be verified before reading the result.

Moving from R&D growth to the five-year R&D capital stock is a substantive change with a documented value channel, but the construction is asymmetric — the short leg becomes low-R&D firms with *clean* earnings, which the hypothesis never justifies — and scaling R&D capital by assets rather than market value weakens the link to the known intangible-capital premium.

Sign logic is internally consistent, but stripped of the indicator this is simply the Sloan accrual anomaly run on an intan/at > 5% subsample — a sample filter, not a new mechanism — and the closely related conditional accrual bet (AccrualBetGatedByRnDIntensity) already failed in the archive at t = 0.38.

A defensible broadening of the archive's best-performing bet leg (adding purchased intangibles so acquisition-built firms are not mis-scored as zero), but it changes two things at once — the intangible measure *and* the switch from ZSCORE to IND_ZSCORE — so a change in alpha will not be attributable to either, and the added `intan` stock is a book-value item that the "missing from book value" mechanism explicitly does not apply to.

A genuine single-lever ablation (1-year vs 3-year accrual gate) on the archive's strongest mechanism, with an interpretable outcome either way — persistence of earnings quality versus transient accrual reversal — and no sign or coverage inconsistency.

Sign and construction are internally consistent and the industry-relative gate with zero-fill genuinely repairs the 4.7% coverage of the gen-0 winner, but because IND_RANK is a strictly positive [0,1] weight applied to raw accruals across essentially the full universe, the signal risks loading heavily on plain Sloan accruals — the proposal should be judged against a vanilla-accrual benchmark, not against zero.

Substituting a firm-relative (time-series rank) accrual frame for the cross-sectional level is the one dimension the archive has never varied and separates business-model accrual intensity from transitory accounting discretion; the main caveat is that TS_RANK over five annual observations is a very coarse statistic and may be dominated by ties and noise.

A legitimate out-of-channel replication that would discriminate between "expensed intangible capital" and "R&D/tech-specific" explanations, but `COALESCE(xad, 0)` converts a reporting decision into an economic zero for the majority of firms, so the bet leg will behave largely as an advertiser/non-advertiser indicator and any result will be confounded with the known advertising-expenditure anomaly.

Since RANK(NEG(x)) ≈ 1 − RANK(x) and the accrual leg is identical to the archived signal's, this expression is algebraically ≈ AcquiredIntangibleAccrualInflation minus the plain working-capital accrual z-score — so it is a linear combination of an already-evaluated signal and vanilla Sloan accruals rather than a new corner of the joint distribution, and the "impairment" leg is in practice dominated by routine amortization.

This is a mechanical recombination of two archived signals (BroadIntangibleCapitalCleanAccruals' bet leg with ChronicCleanAccrualIntangibleCapital's gate) whose own stated hypothesis predicts dilution, so it is an ablation of the current best signal rather than a new economic bet.

A single-operator swap (ZSCORE→IND_ZSCORE) on the archived best signal is a cosmetic variant, and the archive already contains both industry-demeaned and raw versions of adjacent constructs from which the sector-tilt question could largely be answered.

Besides being a pure denominator ablation of the archived winner, scaling by ceq is internally hazardous — negative or near-zero book equity flips the sign of the intangible-capital measure for exactly the distressed, heavily-expensing firms the hypothesis targets, and 1% winsorization does not repair a sign inversion.

The reasoning is internally honest (correctly noting the outer RANK is monotone and thus leaves decile alphas identical, isolating the FMB-attenuation question), and the one substantive change — 3-year accrual smoothing carried to the negative-side leader — is a defensible, economically motivated port, though the incremental content over WithinIndustryIntangibleGatedAccruals is modest.

This is the first output-based (return-on-intangible-capital) leg in the family and the R&D-capitalized denominator is a coherent comparability fix, but be aware the bet leg is close to Novy-Marx gross profitability with a Peters–Taylor style denominator, so any alpha must be shown to exceed what plain GP/AT plus an accrual gate already delivers.

The hard gate is miscalibrated because ib − oancf is negative for the large majority of firms (depreciation alone drives it below zero), so "conservative accruers" is not a selective subsample, and zeroing the remainder creates a huge mass of tied observations that will make the middle decile portfolios arbitrary and the FMB slope hard to interpret.

This is a functional-form swap (MUL→MIN) on an already-tested gen-3 signal whose two legs reduce, once the near-inert intangible-augmented denominator is stripped away, to the well-known gross-profitability × accruals pairing (Novy-Marx + Sloan), so it is more a cosmetic recombination of archive winners than a new mechanism.

A defensible incremental composite that keeps all legs on a bounded scale, but the pre-R&D-earnings and clean-accrual gates are mechanically correlated (both are functions of ib), so the third gate may add little beyond thinning the long leg — worth one test, not a strong prior.

The SUB-of-MINs construction genuinely cancels the intangible main effect and delivers an accrual spread scaled by intangible depth, making it the family's sharpest falsification test of whether the alpha is a true interaction rather than an R&D tilt plus a Sloan tilt; the earlier failed version used materially different inputs, so the retest is informative, though the signal is near-zero for most firms and will concentrate its bet in the tails.

Because MIN is not symmetric under negation (min(1−a,1−b)=1−max(a,b)), this genuinely isolates the "both-bad" corner rather than mirroring the archive's best long signal, the expected negative sign matches the expression's direction, and it plausibly converts the family's diffuse short-side alpha into cross-sectional evidence by replacing a fat-tailed signed z-score with bounded ranks.

It is close to a rediscovery of cash-based operating profitability (Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev) with an R&D-capitalized denominator, and the stated rationale is internally wrong — gross profit (sale−cogs) never deducted R&D, so "adding R&D back" does not undo any expensing distortion but simply bolts an R&D-intensity tilt onto the numerator.

A clean single-lever diagnostic on the archive's best construct that would meaningfully distinguish within-industry mispricing from an unpriced sector tilt, though it is incremental by design and, if it works, mostly reinterprets rather than extends the existing result.

This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested levers (triple gate × IND_RANK) rather than a new mechanism, and the stated motivation misreads the archive — industry-relative ranking *lowered* both the alpha (6.2%→4.6%) and the ls_talpha (4.48→4.00), so there is no demonstrated "lift" to combine.

The diagnosis (large multiplicative alpha with a dead FMB slope suggests fat-tailed z-score weighting) is coherent and the fix — recasting the internal-minus-acquired leg into the bounded conjunctive form that has worked elsewhere — is a substantive, sign-consistent test rather than a cosmetic reparameterization.

The expression is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis because R&D expense is a cash operating outflow already deducted inside oancf, so SUB(oancf, xrd) double-subtracts research spending rather than measuring "cash left after paying for R&D," and the remaining gate is close to the well-known cash-based operating profitability anomaly.

The construction is orientation-consistent with the negative expected sign and plausibly repairs the family's weak short leg, but the resulting short portfolio (intangible-heavy, unprofitable pre-R&D, accrual-supported) is close to a generic junk/distress screen, so a significant result may add little beyond the profitability and accrual anomalies already known.
This is a pure lookback-window tweak (MA 3 → MA 5) of ConjunctiveIntangibleEarningsQuality with no new economic content, exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective asks to avoid.

Swapping the pre-R&D ROA gate for a revenue-side margin gate is a genuine test of whether the triple-gate gain comes from profitability information generally or from the ib-sharing bottom-line channel, though unadjusted gross margin is strongly industry-determined and an IND_RANK version would be the cleaner comparison.

This is a gate-swap recombination of two archived constructs (TwoCornerIntangibleAccountingSpread and PreResearchCashGenerationIntangibleCapital) rather than a new mechanism, and the short corner double-counts oancf because the chronic-accrual term (ib − oancf) and the NEG(oancf+xrd) term move together by construction, so the "clean statement about cash-versus-accounting provenance" is partly mechanical.

A legitimate and cheap diagnostic on whether the two best gates are complementary, but the claim that they are "economically distinct" is overstated since both are dominated by the same oancf term, so the most likely outcome is a thinner long leg with essentially the same alpha as the better single gate.

Applying a three-year moving average to the gate of the archive's best signal is a one-parameter cosmetic variant, and while the horizon-matching argument is coherent, it does not constitute the substantively different improvement the objective calls for.

The stated rationale — that the three conditions now come from three different financial statements and are therefore independent — is internally inconsistent, since the accrual gate is literally ib − oancf and the new cash gate is oancf + xrd, so it replaces one shared-term overlap (ib) with another (oancf) rather than removing it.

Changing the R&D accumulation window from five years to three is a trivial parameter sweep on an existing signal, and the coverage argument is unlikely to hold because COALESCE(xrd,0) means the 0.091 coverage floor is set by other inputs, not by the R&D history requirement.

The expression contradicts the hypothesis: DELTA(wcap) = Δ(act − lct) includes changes in cash and in current debt, so a firm converting research into cash and holding it registers as *rising* working capital and is penalized, exactly inverting the intended "converting research into cash" reading — the noncash, debt-excluded accrual construction (already used in AcquiredIntangibleAccrualInflation) is required for the stated mechanism.

This is a leg-swap on the already-evaluated TwoCornerIntangibleAccountingSpread — the long corner is verbatim CashAndAccrualDoubleGatedIntangibleCapital and the short corner is verbatim UnprofitableAccrualSupportedIntangibleFirms — so the output is close to a mechanical linear combination of two archived signals with a largely predictable result, and any alpha gain will be hard to attribute to new economics rather than to double-counting the same oancf-based earnings-quality gate on both sides.

The Sloan-style balance-sheet reconstruction of operating cash flow is a legitimate, textbook fill rather than an arbitrary coverage patch and the coverage diagnostic (0.091 for oancf-based versus 0.121 for balance-sheet-only signals with the same xrd requirement) supports the binding-constraint claim, but this is a sample-extension robustness test of PreResearchCashGenerationIntangibleCapital rather than a new mechanism, and it risks a regime break because the reconstructed series omits non-dp non-cash items and applies mostly to the pre-1988 sample.

The motivating diagnosis is factually wrong — MIN of continuous RANK values produces no point mass or tied floor, so the claimed "large tied mass" explanation for the FMB/alpha sign conflict is unfounded — leaving this as a bare MIN-to-SUMRANK functional-form swap on an archived signal with no substantive economic revision.

A defensible best-of-legs consolidation whose outcome is genuinely uncertain (the internal-minus-acquired leg delivered strong alpha but weak FMB slopes in both prior forms, so whether goodwill netting survives the cash gate is informative), though the subtraction of two raw asset-scaled ratios inside a single RANK is crude and the incremental novelty over InternalNetAcquiredConjunctiveQuality is modest.

The stock-versus-flow distinction between the NWC/sales level and the annual accrual is a real economic distinction and the level version had the archive's best coverage, but NWC/sales is largely a business-model/industry classifier (it will systematically favor services, software and negative-working-capital retail models) and overlaps mechanically with the cash-generation gate, so an unconditional-industry robustness check is needed before crediting any result.
